Resolve Behaviors

Resolve Behaviors provide a deterministic, centralized mechanism for normalizing incoming state inputs into a canonical upstream value suitable for pipeline processing. The Resolve stage establishes a consistent execution boundary between pipeline admission and downstream computation by classifying and resolving all supported input forms before operators are applied.

State updates may be submitted through the following FeatureCell APIs: replaceState, mergeState and fromStream. Each API admits a different category of input, but all converge on the same Resolve stage for normalization.

The Resolve stage is responsible for identifying the input category associated with each invocation and producing a normalized upstream value that downstream pipeline stages can process consistently.

Supported input forms include:

  • Plain state values and structured state envelopes
  • Deferred factories representing promise-backed resolution, such as functions that initiate network requests, Fetch-based calls, or application-owned API client invocations and resolve asynchronously to a state value.
  • Observable-based inputs that emit a single resolved value for pipeline processing, including Angular HttpClient request streams, RxJS-based data sources, or other observable sequences.
  • Angular HttpResourceRef inputs (Angular-only)
  • Explicit null and undefined inputs

Regardless of the entry point or input form, the Resolve stage guarantees that downstream pipeline stages receive a predictable, normalized upstream value or an explicitly suppressed write.

Resolve Stage

The Resolve Stage is responsible for normalizing incoming state inputs into a canonical upstream value that can be safely processed by downstream pipeline stages. It establishes a strict execution boundary between pipeline admission and computation by ensuring that all supported input forms are resolved into a predictable value shape.

The Resolve Stage executes after interceptors and before operators, filters, reducers, and merge. Each pipeline execution passes through the Resolve Stage exactly once, guaranteeing that downstream stages always operate on a normalized upstream value or an explicitly suppressed write.

Resolve behaviors:

  • Operate exclusively on incoming state inputs
  • Normalize supported input forms into a canonical upstream value
  • Ensure consistent value shape before downstream processing
  • Do not derive new state or modify existing state
  • Do not influence pipeline control flow beyond resolution

Core Pipeline Stage

The Resolve stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle. All required resolve behaviors are installed by default and cannot be omitted. The Resolve stage does not support add-on or user-defined resolve behaviors.

Resolve behaviors do not persist values, emit state, or perform side effects. Their responsibility ends once the incoming input has been normalized and forwarded to downstream pipeline stages.

Accepted State Input Types

The Resolve stage accepts a well-defined set of input forms that represent both synchronous and asynchronous state updates. These input types allow state updates to be expressed uniformly regardless of whether the value is immediately available, produced lazily, emitted over time, or derived from an external resource.

All accepted inputs are normalized by the Resolve stage into a canonical upstream value before any downstream pipeline stages execute. This guarantees that operators, filters, reducers, and state commitment logic always receive a predictable value shape and never need to reason about transport, timing, or source-specific concerns.

Each input form carries explicit semantic intent. Structured envelopes may convey loading or error signals alongside values, deferred factories represent promise-backed resolution, observable-based inputs represent stream-derived values, and explicit undefined or null inputs communicate intentional no-op or state-clearing behavior. These distinctions are preserved through resolution to ensure deterministic pipeline outcomes.
